identity.title: Genome-wide identification and characterization of Arabidopsis domain of unknown function 1995 (DUF1995) gene family.

content.abstract: DUF1995 is an ancient cyanobacteria-originated family. Five Arabidopsis members are leaf-expressed, chloroplast-targeted. LPA3 is essential for chloroplast development and interacts with PSII proteins in yeast; other members require further investigation. The DUF1995 family remains largely functionally unknown. To elucidate its evolutionary dynamics, we performed a genome-wide analysis across 29 key species, representing all major lineages from Cyanobacteria to Angiospermae. We identified 173 DUF1995 family genes across all examined lineages, highlighting its ancient and conserved role in the green lineage. Phylogenetic analysis, with cyanobacterial sequences as the outgroup, revealed that the remaining DUF1995 family proteins formed two major clades. Notably, the five Arabidopsis DUF1995 members were distributed across different subclades within these two clades. Subcellular localization analysis revealed that all five Arabidopsis DUF1995 proteins are targeted to the chloroplast. Consistently, these genes were highly expressed in leaves, as shown by transcript analysis. These findings suggest that DUF1995 family members may play important roles in photosynthesis or other chloroplast-based metabolic processes. We therefore generated CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout lines for all five genes. Except for at1g73060 (lpa3), the other four mutants displayed no obvious phenotypes under normal light. The lpa3 mutant displayed stunted growth and yellow-green leaves. Online interaction analysis indicated that LPA3 interacts with several photosystem II (PSII) proteins. Split-ubiquitin yeast two-hybrid analysis showed that full-length LPA3 interacts with CP43, ALB3, and LPA2. However, this interaction exhibited little conserved similarity across the isolated DUF1995 domains of the five Arabidopsis members. Collectively, these results provide foundational insights into the DUF1995 family and lay the groundwork for further mechanistic research.
